evidence_quotes.quote: About 63% of rural residents do not have access to centralized water supply, heat supply and sewerage systems.

The purpose of the current study was to obtain objective assessments of the level of social and economic well-being of the rural population of the Krasnoyarsk Territory and determine the list of infrastructure facilities, the introduction of which will lead to an improvement in living conditions in rural areas.

The information base for the collection of indicators was formed by data from the Federal Statistics Service for the Krasnoyarsk Territory. To conduct the assessment, an index approach was chosen, the implementation of which was carried out according to the following algorithm.

All these areas have similar characteristics in common: low population density, but high concentration in settlements; the presence of large industrial facilities; the predominance of industrial production and employment; special legal regime (areas are located in the zone of the Far North or areas equated to the Far North).
Inconsistency of housing conditions with the minimum level of improvement (availability of centralized water supply, heat supply, sewerage systems).

criterion_notes.c1: Includes household/municipal housing-improvement indicators for centralized water supply and sewerage non-coverage as 2 of 23 indicators in a rural living-conditions assessment (plus water supply network depreciation and street water/sewer network repair needs).
criterion_notes.c2: Fails BOTH the plain wording and the narrow 2026-10-13 rule-type reading of Criterion 2. Under the plain wording, the study is a descriptive socio-economic and infrastructure index assessment comparing rural municipal districts to urban standards across geographical/climatic groups; its single passing mention that four northern industrial districts have a 'special legal status' / 'special legal regime (areas are located in the zone of the Far North or areas equated to the Far North)' is unanalysed macro-territorial context noted alongside industrial specialization to explain their overall 23-indicator composite index score, with no empirical examination of any legal, administrative, institutional, regulatory, or governance factor or its relationship to water or sanitation access. Under the narrow 2026-10-13 reading, no rule-type mechanism directly governing water or sanitation access (such as eligibility rules, tenure/documentation requirements, tariffs, administrative burden, enforcement, or utility regulatory structure) is studied.
criterion_notes.c3: Empirical descriptive quantitative study using 2019 secondary statistical data from the Federal Statistics Service for the Krasnoyarsk Territory across rural municipal districts to compute normalized composite quality-of-life indices.
criterion_notes.c4: Reports summary descriptive statistics (mean, min, max, median) across rural areas in 2019 for the share of total housing area not equipped with water supply (mean 53.1%) and sewerage (mean 68.4%), water network depreciation (mean 48.8%), and km of street water/sewer networks needing replacement, though district-level comparisons in Table 3 report only the aggregated 23-indicator composite index.
criterion_notes.c5: Population (rural municipal districts and rural residents of Krasnoyarsk Territory) and descriptive statistical index design are identifiable, but no legal/governance exposure is examined in relation to a water or sanitation access outcome (district comparisons aggregate all 23 socio-economic indicators into a single composite index).

study_design: Cross-sectional descriptive statistical and composite index study
population_and_sample: Rural population and rural municipal districts of the Krasnoyarsk Territory, Russia (2019 official regional statistics)
exposure: Rural versus urban benchmark comparison and geographical/climatic municipal district grouping (agrarian versus industrial territorial economies); no legal, administrative, regulatory, or governance exposure analysed
outcome: Composite Index of Living Conditions (ILC) across 23 socio-economic indicators, with region-wide descriptive statistics for housing area not equipped with water supply (mean 53.1%) and sewerage (mean 68.4%), water supply network depreciation (mean 48.8%), and street water/sewer network repair needs
rationale: Excluded under E03 (Wrong exposure). While the paper reports descriptive 2019 official statistics on rural housing lacking centralized water supply and sewerage in the Krasnoyarsk Territory as 2 of 23 indicators in a composite quality-of-life index, it is a general socio-economic and infrastructure assessment comparing rural municipal districts to urban benchmarks across geographical/climatic zones. It examines neither a broad governance/institutional variable nor a narrow rule-type legal/administrative mechanism governing water or sanitation service access; the brief parenthetical reference to the Far North 'special legal regime' of four northern industrial districts is unanalysed background context for their overall 23-indicator composite index score.
